extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students and researchers in analytic and projective geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, theorems, and computational procedures for polar planes, poles, polar lines, polar reciprocal surfaces, and related loci with respect to surfaces of the second degree (quadrics) and special directors (sphere, ellipsoid, paraboloid, cone).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: polar plane and pole
rubrics_metrics.description: The plane given by equation (2) is called the polar plane of the point P(a,y,z) with regard to the surface (1); the point P is called the pole of that plane with respect to that surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text derives the explicit equation of the polar plane (equation (2)) by eliminating parameters; this identification is the basis for subsequent reciprocal relations and computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar plane for a cone through the vertex
rubrics_metrics.description: When the surface (1) is a cone with vertex at the origin (C=C'=C''=E=0), the polar plane of any point with regard to the cone passes through the vertex/centre of the cone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialization of the general polar equation (2) yields a simpler form (2') showing the polar plane always goes through the cone's vertex; used to deduce polar-line relations for cones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar of the centre is at infinity (centre <-> polar plane at infinity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the pole P coincides with the centre of a second-degree surface (the point that bisects every chord through it), then PQ=PQ' so P' is at infinity; hence the polar plane of the centre is at infinity and the coefficients of a,y,z in equation (2) must vanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a system of linear equations whose elimination yields the coordinates of the centre of the surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition / equations to find the centre coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: For the centre (ξ, η, ζ) of surface (1), the coefficients of a,y,z in the polar plane equation vanish, giving linear equations (displayed in text) from which the centre coordinates can be found by elimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtracting those coefficient expressions from the general polar coefficients produces explicit linear relations useful in computational determination of the centre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar planes of points on same diameter are parallel
rubrics_metrics.description: By assigning different points on the same diameter, the resulting polar planes are parallel; the polar planes of all points on a diameter form a parallel family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown by expressing polar plane in terms of direction ratios (m,n) of the diameter (equation (4)). For cones this specialization yields equation (4') independent of the pole coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pole at infinity -> polar is diametral plane (bisects chords parallel to direction)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a pole is at infinity the transversal PP' is parallel to a fixed direction; the polar plane is then the diametral plane which bisects all chords parallel to that direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take coordinates with pole at infinity (z∞ = ∞) and simplify equation (4) to obtain the diametral plane equation (6); for spheres this diametral plane is perpendicular to the corresponding diameter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pole outside surface -> polar plane contains contact points of tangent cone
rubrics_metrics.description: If the pole P is outside the surface and one draws the transversal PP' so that it touches the surface, the contact point(s) belong to the polar plane of P; the enveloping cone tangent to the surface has its curve of contact lying in the polar plane of the vertex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This links geometric constructions (tangent cones) to algebraic polar-plane membership: contact points of an enveloping cone are contained in the polar plane of its vertex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pole on surface <-> polar plane is the tangent plane at the pole
rubrics_metrics.description: When the pole P lies on the surface (i.e., a specific condition/vanishing polynomial is satisfied), the polar plane (2) becomes the tangent plane to the surface at P; equivalently the polar plane passes through its pole iff it touches the surface at that point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives the explicit algebraic condition (displayed) equivalent to tangency; this is used to detect and compute tangent planes from polar equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity theorem for points and polar planes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the polar plane of any point P passes through a second point R, then reciprocally the polar plane of R passes through P; such points are called polar reciprocal points with respect to the given surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fundamental symmetric relation underlies the notion of poles and polars and is proved by comparing the polar-plane equations of the two points (equations (7) and the polar equation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar reciprocal straight lines (for cones)
rubrics_metrics.description: If OP and OR are straight lines through the vertex O of a cone such that the polar plane of OP passes through OR, then reciprocally the polar plane of OR passes through OP; such pairs of lines are polar reciprocal straight lines with respect to the cone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text extends point-plane reciprocity to straight lines through the cone vertex; intersections of polar lines and planes are used to construct reciprocal objects (see subsequent paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar line of a plane (with respect to a cone)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a given plane (4') with respect to cone (1'), the polar line is the straight line (5) passing through the vertex and consisting of all possible poles of planes parallel to (4'). The polar line is the locus conjugate to that plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic elimination gives the polar line equations; geometrically the polar line is the intersection of the cone conjugate to the plane, and may be obtained by examining planes passing through the vertex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus of poles of planes through a given straight line => reciprocal polar straight line
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a straight line (8), the locus of poles of all planes passing through that line is another straight line (9); lines (8) and (9) are reciprocal polars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure: set plane coefficients to satisfy passing-through-line conditions, substitute pole-formula relations and eliminate to get parametric equations of the locus of poles (see displayed elimination leading to (9)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: compute coordinates of the pole of a given plane (elimination formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given plane az+by+cz=1 (equation (10)), the coordinates of its pole (x',y',z') are determined by solving three linear relations involving the quadratic-surface coefficients and auxiliary determinants N, N', N", D (equations (11) and the definitions (0)-(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text supplies explicit determinant-like combinations N,N',N",D built from surface coefficients to compute the pole; simplifications are given when the plane coincides with coordinate planes, producing poles of coordinate planes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: polar reciprocal surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Two surfaces (A) and (B) are polar reciprocals with respect to a director surface (C) if points of (A) are poles of tangent planes to (B) and reciprocally points of (B) are poles of tangent planes to (A), relative to C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tangent planes of B at Q,Q',... intersect at R, R is the pole of the plane through corresponding P,P',...; by continuity the correspondence between tangent planes and poles produces the reciprocal surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tangent plane <-> conjugate diametral plane relation (director-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a tangent plane is applied at a point of surface B and a diameter of the director C is drawn through the corresponding point of A, then the diametral plane of C conjugate to that diameter is parallel to the tangent plane. For a central director with centre at origin this simplifies: tangent plane to B is parallel to the diametral plane of C conjugate to corresponding radius of A. For a sphere director the tangent plane is perpendicular to the corresponding radius vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This geometric relation lets one deduce directions of tangent planes from the director's conjugate diameters; sphere specialization yields orthogonality useful in many constructions (sphero-polar reciprocity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure: find reciprocal surface relative to ellipsoid/hyperboloid/paraboloid director
rubrics_metrics.description: Given surface (B) and a director of second degree, form the polar-plane-identification equations (three relations equating tangent-plane coefficients to polar-plane coefficients) and eliminate the coordinates of corresponding points to obtain the equation of the reciprocal surface (method described at length in No. XXVII and following).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives full algebraic systems (equations (3),(3'), etc.), and shows simplifications for homogeneous forms (use Euler's theorem) and for special directors (sphere, central surfaces, paraboloid) with worked examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: reciprocal of an ellipsoid with sphere director
rubrics_metrics.description: If the director is a concentric sphere and the given surface is an ellipsoid (equation (11)), its reciprocal surface is another ellipsoid whose axes are reciprocally proportional to those of the given one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation uses differentiation and the simplified polar-identities for a sphere director (equations (10)-(12)); consequence used in wave theory of light.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal of an envelope-of-planes (moving plane law)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a surface B is the envelope of a family of planes parameterized by (l,m,n,v) satisfying a relation W(l,m,n,v)=0 and P+m+n^2=1, then with director taken as the unit sphere the polar reciprocal A can be obtained by substituting l= v x', m= v y', n= v z', v = 1/ρ (ρ reciprocal radius) into W and eliminating to obtain the polar (equation (14)-(16)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields a polar-equation viewpoint: the law of motion of the planes becomes the polar equation of the reciprocal surface; the method is effective when the envelope is given explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volar curve: locus of poles of tangent planes to a developable surface
rubrics_metrics.description: For a developable surface (envelope of a family of planes), the locus of the poles of its tangent planes (relative to a director sphere) is the volar curve; in general it's a space curve of double curvature, but for cones and cylinders it reduces to a plane curve (lying in the polar plane of the vertex or in the diametral plane respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text derives the parametric equations for the locus using identification of the moving plane with the polar plane (equations (21)-(22)) and examples demonstrating quartic plane curves and polar-coordinate forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar curve of a quadric cone (with respect to a sphere) is a conic section
rubrics_metrics.description: The polar curve of a cone of the second degree with respect to a sphere is a conic section: it is the intersection of the cone and a plane (the polar plane) and has geometric focal/circular-section perpendicularity properties described in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic elimination between the tangent-plane and polar-plane equations (equations (25)-(26)) produces the conic; geometric interpretation: the cone having that conic as base and the sphere centre as vertex has focal lines and circular sections with perpendicularity relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar surface of a curve (with respect to a sphere): construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a space curve, the polar surface (relative to a sphere) is obtained by taking at each point the tangent line, forming the polar line of that tangent (via formulas (27)-(28)), and eliminating the local parameter to obtain the polar surface; this is the surface whose tangent planes correspond to points of the given curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text provides explicit equations for tangent and polar-line relations and a worked example for a conic section producing a reciprocal cone (equations (29)-(30)).
